transcription: English research paraphrases of all17 source indicators, visually checked on PDF52–53. These are curriculum indicators, not a city exam rubric or a mastery/completion rule.

items.description_en: Understand topic-related speech and retell it using key words and visual cues
Use discourse clues to predict, identify speaker roles and infer feelings, attitudes and viewpoints
Understand major content and key information in multimodal material
Obtain and compare basic cultural information from books and audiovisual material
Use basic word formation to infer unfamiliar meanings in context
Use reading strategies and organising tools to identify main information and gist
Read longer material, infer implicit information, offer views and ask reasoned questions
Read short topic-related passages aloud with natural pace and pauses and broadly accurate pronunciation and intonation
Choose initially appropriate language for the situation to express feelings, attitudes and views
Use appropriate words, patterns and tenses to describe people and things orally or in writing
Introduce cultural phenomena briefly through spoken or written discourse
Tell the stories of representative outstanding people coherently
Write using learned language with reasonably conventional formats
Imitate brief models such as replies to letters accurately and appropriately
Use picture and text prompts to complete, continue or adapt passages
Gather information through varied channels and examine linguistic and cultural material from different perspectives
Participate in learning activities and cooperate with peers on theme-related tasks
